title: Telemetry-gated suggestion propagator with operator acknowledgement
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Build a telemetry-gated propagation service that automatically applies Optimize batching and caching recommendations to customer scopes in a phased, observable way while requiring explicit operator acknowledgement when thresholds are exceeded. This task is to design and implement the runtime propagation engine, a policy DSL for gating, and the operator acknowledgement flow wired into Console and the rollout controller.

Goals:
- Reduce manual toil by safely applying low-risk Optimize recommendations (prefetch caches, batch sizes, kv-cache reuse) to eligible routes.
- Prevent broad blast radius via telemetry gates and explicit operator acknowledgement for anything beyond low-risk changes.
- Provide clear observability and fast rollback triggers based on production signals.

Success metrics:
- 60% of low-risk recommendations auto-applied without human intervention in pilot customers.
- Zero-severity incidents caused by applied suggestions during the pilot (operational rollback within 10 minutes if triggered).
- Time-to-apply for approved suggestions reduced from manual ~2 hours to automated ~2 minutes for gate-passed cases.

Design overview:
We will introduce a lightweight "propagator" service that receives Optimize suggestions, evaluates them against a policy DSL (policy defined per-customer or per-org), executes a staged application plan (phases: dry-run, canary, broad), and registers telemetry gates that continuously monitor signals such as p95 latency, error budget burn, token QPS, and model mismatch rate. The propagator will attach a short-lived rollout token and create a RolloutRecord in the Console to track state and to enable operator acknowledgement in the dashboard.

Gating policy primitives:
- risk_level: enum [low, medium, high]
- signals: list of telemetry signals with thresholds (p95_latency_increase_pct, error_rate_delta, token_cost_delta)
- canary_fraction: numeric (0.01 - 0.5)
- require_ack_for: list of change types (e.g., quantization, cross-model-fallback, aggressive-batching)

Canary policy behavior:
- For low-risk changes: dry-run then immediate canary at customer-configured fraction. If telemetry remains healthy for N minutes, auto-progress to broad application.
- For medium/high risk or any changes in require_ack_for: stop after dry-run and surface for operator acknowledgement in Console. Operator can approve with a comment or adjust canary_fraction.

Operator acknowledgement flow:
- Console shows a pending RolloutRecord with diff, estimated cost delta, and a compact telemetry simulation summary (based on recent traces).
- Operator actions: Approve (start canary), Approve+Force (bypass policy, logged), Request Changes (sends back to Optimize suggestions for revision), or Reject.
- Approvals create audit log entries and trigger an infra event that arms the propagator to start canary.

Rollback & rollback triggers:
- Automated rollback triggers if any of the following occur during canary/broad: p95 latency increases > 30% compared to baseline, error rate increases > 0.5 percentage points, SLO burn rate > 2x baseline for 5m.
- If triggered, propagator flips the rollout to REVERTING, signals Console, notifies on-call via PagerDuty, and marks the suggestion as "reverted by telemetry" with attached traces.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative defaults reduce immediate cost savings but minimize risk; we will surface tradeoffs in Console and allow customers/operators to relax policies.
- Doing richer simulation (token-level replay) is useful but costly; initial iteration uses lightweight statistical simulation + sampling traces.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Optimize suggestions API (ingest endpoint) -> Propagator -> Rollout controller -> Serving config applier.
- Console UI changes for RolloutRecords, operator acknowledgement, and diffs.
- Telemetry: Grafana dashboards + alerts + rollout-level tracing.

Links to artifacts:
- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/123456/Telemetry+Gated+Propagation+PRD
- Design sketch: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xExampleDesign/view
- Telemetry schema doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/telemetry/rollouts

Notes: this ticket focuses on the propagator service and acknowledgement wiring; separate follow-ups will handle full Console UX polish and customer self-serve policy editor.
acceptance_criteria: Propagator can receive Optimize suggestions and evaluate them against a per-customer policy
Dry-run simulation produces a stable diff and estimated cost delta shown in a RolloutRecord
Low-risk suggestions proceed to canary automatically and record telemetry during canary
Medium/high-risk suggestions require operator acknowledgement in Console before canary
Automated rollback triggers and reverts applied configs when thresholds breached, with audit log entries
Integration test coverage for end-to-end path: ingest -> policy -> canary -> commit/revert
steps: Implement policy DSL parser and evaluator in propagator service
Add dry-run simulation module using sampled traces and statistical estimation
Create RolloutRecord proto and wire to Console APIs
Implement canary executor that updates serving configs for canary fraction and collects telemetry
Wire automated rollback logic with defined thresholds and PagerDuty hooks
Write end-to-end tests and run pilot with 3 internal customers
